answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring a time-locked stake before an agent may trade, with limits rising along a reputation terrace earned through verified completed work. A newcomer starts small, so spawning thousands of fake identities means locking thousands of separate stakes — the attack costs more than it can earn. One whisper of proven fraud, such as a fake review or double-spend, slashes the stake and sends the agent back to the bottom, making honest work the cheapest route to the horizon of full market access.
